title: Test doubles: stubs, spies, mocks and fakes in Vitest
objectives: Name the job a double does in a test — stub, spy, mock or fake — and pick the one that asserts least about how the code works
Use `vi.fn`, `vi.spyOn` and `mockResolvedValue`/`mockImplementation`, and undo what you replaced (Vitest 4's `restoreAllMocks` only restores `vi.spyOn` spies)
Explain why `vi.mock` is hoisted above imports, and fix a factory that reads an outer variable (`vi.hoisted`) or drops exports (`importOriginal`)
Drive time with fake timers, and use `advanceTimersByTimeAsync` when the code awaits between timers
Spot over-mocking, and replace the network with MSW instead of stubbing your own client

sources.title: Vitest 4 docs: Migrating to Vitest 4 (mock changes)
Mock Service Worker docs: Node.js integration

questions.prompt: A test of `checkout` passes an `InMemoryOrders` class whose `save` and `find` really store and return orders in a `Map`, then reads the saved order back. What job is that double doing?

options.text: A fake — a working implementation with a shortcut, checked by the state it ends up in
A stub — it returns canned answers
A spy — it records how it was called
A mock — the expected calls are the assertion

questions.explanation: It really works — save then find returns what you saved — just without Postgres. That's a fake, and the test asserts on outcomes (the stored order), which survives refactors. A stub returns fixed answers whatever you do to it; a spy or mock is about the calls, not the resulting state.

questions.prompt: A test does `const spy = vi.spyOn(console, "error")` and then triggers an error path. What happens to the output?

options.text: It still prints — `spyOn` calls the original by default; add `.mockImplementation(() => {})` to silence it
It's silenced — spying replaces the method with a no-op
`spyOn` throws because `console.error` is a built-in
It's buffered and printed only if the test fails

questions.explanation: Vitest's docs: `vi.spyOn` wraps an existing method and the original implementation still works by default. You get the call log; you keep the behaviour. Chain a `mock…` method to replace it, and `mockRestore()` afterwards so the real `console.error` comes back for later tests.

questions.prompt: A test file has `const fetchUserMock = vi.fn();` followed by `vi.mock("./api", () => ({ fetchUser: fetchUserMock }));`, and fails to load with `ReferenceError: Cannot access 'fetchUserMock' before initialization`. Why?

options.text: `vi.mock` is hoisted above everything, so its factory runs before `fetchUserMock` is declared; create it with `vi.hoisted`
`vi.mock` must come before the `const` line in the source
The factory must be `async`
The path `./api` can't be resolved from the test file

questions.explanation: Vitest moves `vi.mock` to the top of the file (before the imports) so the code under test sees the mocked module. That moves the factory above the `const` too, so it runs while `fetchUserMock` is in its temporal dead zone. Reordering the source changes nothing — the call is hoisted anyway. `vi.hoisted(() => ({ fetchUserMock: vi.fn() }))` creates the value in the hoisted region.

questions.prompt: `vi.mock("./api", () => ({ fetchUser: vi.fn() }))`. The code under test also uses `formatDate` from `./api`, and Vitest 4 throws `No "formatDate" export is defined on the "./api" mock`. The fix?

options.text: Spread the real module in: `vi.mock(import("./api"), async (importOriginal) => ({ ...(await importOriginal()), fetchUser: vi.fn() }))`
`vi.spyOn` on `formatDate` as well
Nothing; Vitest falls back to the real `formatDate` for missing keys
Import `formatDate` before calling `vi.mock`

questions.explanation: A factory's return value *is* the module, so anything it doesn't return doesn't exist for the code under test — Vitest doesn't fall back to the real export, it throws. `importOriginal` gives you the real module to spread, and you override only what you need to. Import order is irrelevant because `vi.mock` is hoisted.

questions.prompt: `retry(fn)` awaits `fn()`, and on failure awaits `sleep(1000)` before trying again. `fn` fails twice, then succeeds. With fake timers, the test calls `vi.advanceTimersByTime(2000)` and finds `fn` was called once. Why?

options.text: The retry's `sleep` timer is only scheduled after a microtask, so when the synchronous advance runs there's no timer to fire; use `await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(2000)`
Fake timers also freeze promises, so the rejection never arrives
2000 ms isn't enough; advance by 3000 ms
`sleep` captured the real `setTimeout` before the fake clock was installed

questions.explanation: `advanceTimersByTime` is synchronous: it fires timers that exist *now*. The first rejection is handled in a later microtask, and only then does `sleep` call `setTimeout`. The Async variant lets pending promise callbacks run between timers, so the backoff timers get created and fired — 3 calls. Fake timers never replace native promises (and Vitest 4 leaves `queueMicrotask` and `nextTick` real by default), and a longer advance hits the same empty queue.

questions.prompt: In Vitest 4, `afterEach(() => vi.restoreAllMocks())`. Which of these does it undo?

options.text: Spies made with `vi.spyOn` get their original methods back; `vi.fn()` implementations and call history are left alone
Every mock's implementation, call history and spied method
Only call history
Spied methods plus anything replaced with `vi.stubGlobal`

questions.explanation: Vitest 4 narrowed `restoreAllMocks`: it restores originals for `vi.spyOn` spies and no longer clears history or resets `vi.fn` implementations. Use `vi.clearAllMocks()` for history, `vi.resetAllMocks()` for implementations, and `vi.unstubAllGlobals()` for `stubGlobal`. (Vitest 5 also turns the `clearMocks` config on by default.)

questions.prompt: A `checkout` test replaces rates, orders and mailer with `vi.fn()`s and asserts each was called with exact arguments, in order. Someone caches the exchange rate and the test goes red, though every receipt is identical. What's the real problem?

options.text: The test mocks the code's own collaborators and asserts its call sequence, so it can only pass for this implementation; use a fake store and assert outcomes
The mocks weren't reset between tests
Caching the rate is a bug; the test caught it
`vi.spyOn` should have been used instead of `vi.fn`

questions.explanation: If behaviour is unchanged and the test fails, the test is checking implementation. Replace only what you can't run (network, clock, email), use a fake for your own storage and assert the stored order, and check calls only where the call is the feature ("one receipt email to this address"). Switching to `spyOn` would keep the same over-specified assertions.

questions.prompt: Why intercept requests with MSW (`setupServer`) rather than `vi.stubGlobal("fetch", vi.fn())`?

options.text: Your real client code runs — URL building, headers, the `res.ok` check, JSON parsing — and only the network is replaced
MSW is faster because it skips JSON parsing
Vitest can't stub `fetch` in Node
MSW starts a real HTTP server, so the test is end-to-end

questions.explanation: A stubbed `fetch` returns whatever object you hand it, skipping your own request and response handling — exactly where bugs like a wrong path or a missing `res.ok` check live. MSW intercepts at the network layer inside the test process (no real server), and `onUnhandledRequest: "error"` fails any request no handler expected. Vitest's docs recommend it for request mocking.

prompts.prompt: Stub the async exchange rate, then assert the receipt with the matcher that checks arguments.
code: await checkout(order, { rates: { get: getRate }, mailer: { send } });
prompts.explanation: `mockResolvedValue(v)` makes every call return `Promise.resolve(v)` — the stub's job. `toHaveBeenCalledWith` passes if any call had exactly those arguments; with one call, `toHaveBeenLastCalledWith` says the same thing.

prompts.prompt: Silence and record `console.error` for one test, then put the real one back.
prompts.explanation: `vi.spyOn` wraps the existing method; `mockImplementation` swaps in a no-op so the test output stays clean. `mockRestore()` puts the original back — skip it and every later test in the file has a silent `console.error`.

prompts.prompt: Create the mock in the hoisted region so the hoisted factory can use it.
prompts.explanation: `vi.hoisted` is hoisted along with `vi.mock` and returns its callback's result, so the variable exists by the time the factory runs. A plain top-level `const` would still be uninitialised.

prompts.prompt: Replace only `fetchUser` and keep every other export of the real module.
prompts.explanation: `importOriginal` is asynchronous — it returns a promise of the real module — so it must be awaited before spreading. Spreading the promise itself would copy no exports at all.

prompts.prompt: Install the fake clock and advance it in a way that lets the retry's awaited backoff timers fire.
prompts.explanation: The Async variant flushes pending promise callbacks between timers, so each `await sleep(...)` gets to schedule its timer before the clock moves past it. Pair `useFakeTimers` with `useRealTimers()` in `afterEach`.

code: const sleep = (ms: number) => new Promise<void>((r) => setTimeout(r, ms));
catch (err) { if (attempt >= 3) throw err; await sleep(1000); }
snippets.question: What does it print (Vitest 4)?
snippets.explanation: The first call happens synchronously inside `retry`. Its rejection is handled in a microtask, and only then does `sleep` schedule a timer — after the synchronous `advanceTimersByTime(2000)` has already returned with nothing to fire. With `await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(2000)` it prints 3.

snippets.question: What does it print under Vitest 4?
snippets.explanation: `restoreAllMocks` put the original `api.now` back, so it returns `"real"` — but in Vitest 4 it no longer clears history (the spy still remembers 1 call) and leaves `vi.fn` mocks alone (`impl` keeps its `mockReturnValue` override). Vitest 3.2 printed `real 0 impl` here: it also cleared every spy's history and reset every mock. In Vitest 4 those jobs belong to `clearAllMocks` and `resetAllMocks`.
